title: One-column extension of a prescribed Cartan–Eilenberg boundary comparison
statement: Let $A,B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], $F:A\to B$ exact and additive, $K,L$ complexes indexed by $\mathbf Z$, and $u:F(K)\to L$ a chain map. Let $I,J$ be bicomplexes with horizontal index $\mathbf Z$ and resolution index $\mathbf N$ [def-sp-double-complex-total], augmented by $e_I:K[0]\to I$ and $e_J:L[0]\to J$. Fix $p\in\mathbf Z$ and $q=p+1$. Assume the augmented original-object, cycle, boundary and homology columns in degree $p$, and the outgoing boundary column $\operatorname{Im}(d^{q-1,q})$, are quasi-isomorphisms. Assume the corresponding terms of $J$ are injective [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Put $\varepsilon_I^r=\mathrm{singleObjXSelf}^{-1}\circ(e_I^r)^0$ and define $\varepsilon_J^r$ similarly, and $G=F$ applied to resolution complexes. Given a chain map $b:G(\operatorname{Im}(d_I^{p-1,p}))\to\operatorname{Im}(d_J^{p-1,p})$ with $b^0 F(\operatorname{factorThruImage}(d_I^{p-1,p})^0\varepsilon_I^{p-1})=\operatorname{factorThruImage}(d_J^{p-1,p})^0\varepsilon_J^{p-1}u^{p-1}$, there exist chain maps $x:G(I^p)\to J^p$ and $c:G(\operatorname{Im}(d_I^{q-1,q}))\to\operatorname{Im}(d_J^{q-1,q})$ such that $x^0F(\varepsilon_I^p)=\varepsilon_J^pu^p$, $c$ obeys the same boundary augmentation equation at $q$, $xG(\operatorname{image.\iota}(d_I^{p-1,p}))=\operatorname{image.\iota}(d_J^{p-1,p})b$, and $cG(\operatorname{factorThruImage}(d_I^{q-1,q}))=\operatorname{factorThruImage}(d_J^{q-1,q})x$, identifying columns $p=q-1$ with the displayed eqToHom maps. No comparisons in other original-object columns or boundedness hypotheses are asserted.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ce-comparison-cycle-stage] to obtain an augmented cycle map $y$ whose incoming equation is stated after precomposition with toCycles.
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ce-comparison-object-stage] to $y$, obtaining the augmented object map $x$ that commutes with the cycle inclusions.

In the category of resolution complexes, the sequence $0\to Z^p(I)\to I^p\to\operatorname{Im}(d_I^{p,q})\to0$ is short exact: the first map is the kernel of the differential, the last its image factor, and exactness is reflected across the monomorphic image inclusion. Apply $G$ to this short exact sequence. Since the cycle square implies that $x$ followed by the target outgoing image factor kills the source cycle inclusion, the cokernel universal property constructs $c$ with $G(\operatorname{factorThruImage}(d_I^{p,q}))c=x\operatorname{factorThruImage}(d_J^{p,q})$, in diagrammatic composition order. Thus no further comparison existence statement is needed for $c$.

Precompose the desired incoming image.\iota square with the preserved epimorphism $G(\operatorname{factorThruImage}(d_I^{p-1,p}))$. Rewrite the differential as toCycles followed by iCycles, use the object cycle square, then the cycle-stage incoming square. Cancel this epimorphism to prove the incoming image square.

Evaluate the defining cokernel equation for $c$ in resolution degree zero and precompose with the mapped object augmentation. The augmented object equation for $x$ gives the outgoing boundary augmentation equation. Use $q-1=p$ to identify the displayed transports. Together with the object augmentation and incoming image square, these are exactly the four conclusions.
